subject: Clearline packaging: upgrade path, bundle options, and limited concession
messages:
From: Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwood.com>
To: Sara Lin <sara.lin@clearlinehealth.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-12T09:12:00Z
Subject: Clearline packaging: upgrade path, bundle options, and limited concession

Hi Sara — great to meet you on Friday. Per our conversation I pulled together two concrete packaging paths that align with Clearline's usage profile and compliance needs. High level: 1) Throughput-first (recommended) — reserved Dedicated pool with burst credits; 2) Modular seats + add-on feature bundles — lower commitment, higher unit cost.

Attached: clearline_quote_v2.pdf (side-by-side pricing) and bundle-matrix-aug12.xlsx (feature mapping). Key questions: can procurement sign to 12-month term for dedicated pricing? If not, we can offer a modular bundle with a 6-month pilot and scaled credits.

Next steps: — please confirm whether you prefer predictability (dedicated) or flexibility (modular). — If predictability, I'll request an approval lane for a one-time concession for onboarding credits. Happy to jump on a short call tomorrow to walk through the numbers.

Thanks,
Ethan
Ethan Park
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1-415-555-0192

Attachment stubs: clearline_quote_v2.pdf (PDF, 243KB), bundle-matrix-aug12.xlsx (Excel, 96KB)

From: Sara Lin <sara.lin@clearlinehealth.com>
To: Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@clearlinehealth.com>
Date: 2026-08-12T16:04:00Z
Subject: Re: Clearline packaging: upgrade path, bundle options, and limited concession

Thanks Ethan — that summary is helpful. A couple quick clarifying points: 1) Our CFO prefers no more than 6-month firm commitments for new vendors unless there's a clear runway to ROI. 2) We need clarification on which features are in the "security bundle" vs the "performance bundle" — specifically KPIs around 95th percentile latency and audit log retention.

On discounts: we have an internal target of 18%+ on first-year vendor T&Cs for anything above $150k ARR. Would Redwood be open to a first-year concession (credits/discount) to hit that threshold if we sign to a 12-month auto-renew? If that's a hard ask, can you give a pricing alternative that hits our internal threshold at 6 months?

Also looping procurement for contract language and SOC2 evidence.

Best,
Sara
Director, Product Ops — Clearline Health

--
Sara Lin
Clearline Health
procurement@clearlinehealth.com

From: Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwood.com>
To: Sara Lin <sara.lin@clearlinehealth.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-13T10:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Clearline packaging: upgrade path, bundle options, and limited concession

Sara — thanks for the specifics, this is exactly the kind of framing that helps. Short answers up front: 1) Security vs performance bundles: security bundle includes private VPC control plane, audit logs (13 months retention), and KMS integration; performance bundle includes Dedicated pool + guaranteed 95th pct latency SLO for the configured seq lengths, and prefix caching enabled. I called out the mapping in bundle-matrix-aug12.xlsx (tabs: Security, Performance). 2) Discounting: we can reach your ~18% effective first-year concession in two ways: a) 12-month commitment + 15% list discount + onboarding credits to get to ~18% effective, or b) 6-month pilot with higher onboarding credits but higher per-unit price (effective ~12–14% if you also take a pre-pay option).

I'm attaching a proposed concession language in redlines_clearline.docx — it's a conditional onboarding credit that only triggers upon signed 12-month commitment and usage meeting a minimum throughput band in months 3–6. If you prefer a firm 6-month path, we can move the credit to a usage rebate (paid after month 6).

If procurement wants to see SOC2 folders and evidence, Kimberly can share the package. I'm looped in to coordinate the concession and finalize the quote. Would you be available for a 30-minute pricing call Friday (8/14) at 10am PT?

Cheers,
Ethan

Attachment stubs: redlines_clearline.docx (Word, 48KB)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-13T13:05:00Z
Subject: Clearline concession — internal sign-off request

Ethan / Lauren — quick internal note before we finalize customer-facing language. Clearline is medium risk: mid-market account with good growth signals but procurement wants short firm term. Recommended approach: offer a time-bound 15% list discount + $25k onboarding credit contingent on 12-month term and baseline usage clauses (we protect revenue with minimum throughput). For 6-month pilots, offer $35k onboarding credit but no list discount.

Rationale: putting more credit into the pilot lowers friction while preserving the list price; the 12-month combo gives the customer the financial incentive they want while keeping our NRR profile intact. Lauren — approve the one-off $25k concession from pricing? If approved I'll prepare the doc and updated quote.

Thanks,
Kimberly
Director, Revenue Operations

--
Note: CC to product/legal may be required for special SLA language.

From: Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwood.com>
To: Sara Lin <sara.lin@clearlinehealth.com>, Procurement <procurement@clearlinehealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-14T14:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Clearline packaging: upgrade path, bundle options, and limited concession

Sara — thanks for the clear ask and procurement loop. We ran this internally and can offer the following conditional concession: 1) Option A (12-month commitment): 15% list discount + $25,000 onboarding credit (applied as usage credits over first 3 months) + 95th pct latency SLO in performance bundle. This gets you to ~18% effective first-year concession as requested. 2) Option B (6-month pilot): no list discount, $35,000 onboarding credit as a one-time credit, performance SLO measurable but no long-term SLA.

Security bundle includes 13-month audit log retention and KMS integration; I asked Kimberly to share the SOC2 artifact pack (link below). I've attached an updated quote that reflects Option A numbers and redlined concession language. If Option A is acceptable we'll prepare a short amendment with term and minimum usage band and route for signatures.

Proposed next step: 30-minute call to confirm which option and walk legal/procurement through the concession mechanics. I'm available tomorrow 10am PT or Friday 9am PT.

Links: https://drive.example.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-clearline-pricing (SOC2_artifacts in folder)

Thanks,
Ethan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachment stubs: clearline_quote_v2.pdf, redlines_clearline.docx, bundle-matrix-aug12.xlsx
